user.title: Add to Blink Instant Events
user.description: Local cameras need no account or cloud service; smart detection runs in the Blink Vision add-on on your own hardware.

menu_options.rtsp: RTSP camera (stream address on your network)
menu_options.camera: A camera already in Home Assistant (ONVIF, Generic, …)

blink.title: Sign in to Blink
blink.description: Signs in as a separate Blink app client that receives push notifications. Your password is used once and not stored.

data_description.email: The email address of your Blink account.

2fa.title: Verification code
2fa.description: Enter the PIN Blink just sent you by text or email.

rtsp.title: RTSP camera
rtsp.description: The camera's stream address, e.g. `rtsp://192.168.1.20:554/stream2`. Use its smaller sub-stream if it has one: detection needs little resolution and the Pi decodes it faster. One frame is read to check the address.

data_description.url: rtsp:// or rtsps://. A login in the address is moved to the fields below.
data_description.username: Leave empty if the camera has no login.

camera.title: Camera in Home Assistant
camera.description: For ONVIF cameras, add them with Home Assistant's ONVIF integration first: it discovers them, picks the stream profile and turns their motion events into a binary sensor. Then pick that camera and sensor here.

data_description.motion: When this turns on, a few pictures are analyzed.

vision.title: Blink Vision
vision.description: Only needed when the add-on wasn't found by itself, e.g. the Docker image on another machine.

data_description.vision_token: BLINK_VISION_TOKEN of the container, or the token in the add-on's log.

hassio_confirm.title: Blink Vision
hassio_confirm.description: Use the Blink Vision add-on for smart detection?

error.invalid_pin: The PIN was not accepted. Check it and try again.
error.not_rtsp: Enter an rtsp:// or rtsps:// address.
error.bad_host: The address has no valid host or port.

abort.wrong_account: Sign in with the same Blink account as before.
abort.single_blink_account: A Blink account is already set up; only one is supported.

push_sign_in.title: Sign in for instant events
push_sign_in.description:
Blink only sends instant events to its Android app, so Home Assistant signs in once more, as that app.

1. Open [Blink's sign-in page]({url}) on a computer. Don't use a phone that has the Blink app, because the app would take over the sign-in.
2. Sign in with the same Blink account and enter the code Blink sends you.
3. Blink then goes to a page whose address starts with `{callback}`. The page itself may be blank or show an error. Copy the whole address from the address bar and paste it below.

data.snapshot_after_motion: Take a snapshot after each motion
data.live_look: Look with live view after motion

data_description.snapshot_after_motion: About 30 s after a motion push, ask the camera for a new picture (at most once per camera every 5 minutes). Each one wakes the camera, so it costs battery.
data_description.live_look: For accounts without a Blink subscription, which get no clips. After each motion or doorbell push, watch 8 seconds of live view and let Blink Vision read it. Each look wakes the camera, much like recording a clip does, and starts about 5 seconds after the motion. Skipped while someone is watching the camera.
data_description.vision_url: Leave empty to use the Blink Vision add-on. Set it only if Blink Vision runs somewhere else, e.g. http://192.168.1.20:8000.
data_description.vision_token: Only with a Blink Vision address: the token from the add-on's log or BLINK_VISION_TOKEN.

data_description.keyframes_only: Far less CPU on a Raspberry Pi; motion is seen up to one keyframe interval later.
data_description.sensitivity: How much of the picture must change to count as motion. Raise it if leaves or rain set it off.
data_description.record: Recordings go to the media folder (Media › My media › blink_instant_events). Recording pauses while the disk has under 2 GB free.

error.bad_callback: That isn't the address Blink ended on. It starts with {callback}. Copy it from the same sign-in page this form showed.
error.sign_in_expired: Blink didn't accept that sign-in; it may have expired. Open the new link and sign in again.
error.wrong_account: Sign in with the same Blink account as before.

show_on_tv.name: Show on TV
show_on_tv.description: Plays a camera's live view on a TV or Chromecast, e.g. when the doorbell rings.

media_player.name: TV
media_player.description: The TV. If it is not a Cast device, the Cast device on the same TV is used.

duration.name: Duration
duration.description: Seconds to show it before the TV goes back.

only_if_on.name: Only if the TV is on
only_if_on.description: Do nothing when the TV is off, instead of turning it on.

enroll_face.name: Teach a face
enroll_face.description: Admins only. Teaches Blink Vision this person's face from a camera's current picture or a photo file (one face, close, sharp, facing the camera). Unknown faces are never learned by themselves.

camera.name: Camera
camera.description: Take the photo from this camera now.

file.name: Photo file
file.description: A JPEG or PNG in a folder Home Assistant allows, e.g. /media.

force.name: Even if it looks like someone else
force.description: Keep the photo although it already matches another person.

delete_face.name: Forget a face
delete_face.description: Admins only. Deletes every photo and face feature kept for this person.

process_snapshot.name: Analyze a camera now
process_snapshot.description: Sends any camera's current picture through smart detection and returns what it found (who, what, how sure).

push_sign_in.title: Instant Blink events need one more sign-in
push_sign_in.description: Blink sends motion and doorbell pushes only to its Android app. For {account}, go to Settings › Devices & services › Blink Instant Events › Configure › Sign in for instant events. Until then, motion shows up from polling, every 5 minutes, and doorbell presses don't show up.
